summary.text: 包 means “wrap” or “pack” and can also mean a package or bundle. Shuowen reads the received form as a pregnant figure enclosing an unformed child; a competing origin proposal remains unresolved.

formation.text: The received form has two distinct analyses: Shuowen depicts a pregnant figure enclosing an unformed child, while 字源 reads 勹 as wrapping 巳, together conveying 胞衣, in a semantic construction. Other analyses propose 勹 as a sound component. A competing proposal derives 包 from a separate child-holding graph that first wrote 抱; no dated forms establish that descent. The earliest formation remains unresolved.

components.text: Shuowen depicts 巳 as an unborn child. 字源 instead treats it as the child in a semantic construction with 勹, together conveying 胞衣. These distinct received-form analyses do not settle the earliest graph.
字源 reads 勹 as wrapping 巳 in a semantic construction conveying 胞衣. Other received-form analyses propose a sound role; the earliest function remains unsettled.

sound_limitation.text: The modern Mandarin match does not establish 勹’s historical phonetic role in 包. The Zhengzhang comparison is reported through a reference compilation, not an inspected primary reconstruction publication.

sound.text: Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstruction assigns *pruː to both 勹 and 包, supporting the proposed sound link in that system. These are reconstructed values, not recorded ancient pronunciations.
The 勹 headword gives bāo on 字源 p. 814 (printed p. 801); the separate 包 headword gives bāo on p. 817 (printed p. 804). Matching modern readings do not establish a historical sound role.

history.text: The received-form account preserved in Shuowen and 字源 interprets 包 as pregnancy: 勹 wraps or encloses 巳, understood as an unborn child, together conveying 胞衣. 字源 calls 包 a 会意字. Its labels for script-style forms do not authenticate them as dated artifacts.

A competing proposal links 包 to oracle-bone graphs traditionally read as 保, interpreting them instead as a person holding a child and proposing that 包 first wrote 抱. The proposed link has no dated intermediate forms.

字源’s 包 entry reports that Zhou did not find 包 in the Shang and Western Zhou material he discusses, then infers from its use in the Shijing that it should have existed in the Western Zhou. This is an attributed report of non-attestation and an unverified dating inference, not a verified earliest attestation or artifact chronology; the separate 胞 entry’s estimate concerns 胞, not 包’s component analysis.

uncertainties.text: The traditional pregnancy interpretation, also reflected in 字源’s received-form analysis, and the proposed descent from a child-holding graph are competing accounts. The earliest form and its graphic history remain unresolved; the received-form interpretation does not settle that dispute.

Enclosure and sound are proposed roles for 勹 in received-form analyses; 字源 specifically describes wrapping in a semantic construction. The Zhengzhang comparison supports a sound proposal, but shared fanqie and later interchange do not establish 勹’s role in the earliest formation.
The seal-script-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image, and its correspondence to a primary historical record has not been verified.

senses.period: Current use; classical example is transmitted, but its written-witness date is unresolved
senses.text: 包 is currently used for wrapping, packing, enclosing, or containing. The transmitted Shijing line 白茅包之 is an historical example of wrapping, but its written-witness date is unresolved.
包 is used for a package or bundle as well as for wrapping and packing. The history of this object sense is undated.

limitations.text: The proposal that 包 first wrote 抱 belongs to a disputed account of the graph’s origin; it is not an established, dated earliest meaning. Reported substitutions such as 包 for 苞 or 庖 do not establish the character’s original formation.
Later senses including encompassing, taking responsibility, and guaranteeing are recorded, but no dated sequence connects them to earlier senses.

Pregnancy is the traditional Shuowen interpretation, while wrapping is independently recorded in transmitted examples and current use. The evidence does not establish whether wrapping developed from pregnancy or whether the two are historically unrelated.

relationships.text: In the Shuowen received-form interpretation, 巳 depicts an unformed child; 字源 instead treats it as the semantic part of a 会意 construction with 勹. These are distinct analyses and do not settle the earliest graph.
字源 analyzes 巳 as the unborn child in a semantic 会意 construction with 勹, together conveying 胞衣. This is its received-form interpretation, not an established account of the earliest graph.
Received-form interpretations read 勹 as wrapping or enclosing; 字源 describes it wrapping 巳 in a semantic construction. Other analyses differ on its role, and its earliest function remains unsettled.
Some analyses propose 勹 as a sound component. Zhengzhang reconstructs 勹 and 包 with the same value, but this does not settle 勹’s role in the earliest graph.

overview.text: 包 means ‘wrap’ or ‘pack’ and can name a package or bundle. Its received graph visibly has outer 勹 around inner 巳. Shuowen interpreted these as an enclosing pregnant figure and an unborn child; that reading does not settle the disputed origin.

components.text: In Shuowen’s interpretation, the inner shape represents the unborn child in a pregnant figure; that account does not settle the graph’s earliest origin.
字源 reads 勹 as wrapping the inner child-shape, with the pair conveying 胞衣; other analyses also propose a sound role. The earliest function remains unsettled.

items.period: Shuowen small-seal style; modern redraw, not a dated specimen
items.tradition: Small seal-script style, rendered as a modern vector
items.caption: In this small-seal-style redraw, a curved inner form sits within a larger enclosing outline. Shuowen interpreted the arrangement as an unborn child within a pregnant figure; this received-form reading does not establish the graph’s earliest origin.
items.alt: A curved black form inside a larger enclosing outline, with a short upright stroke above and a long stroke descending from the outline.
items.selection_reason: The inner-and-outer arrangement makes the traditional Shuowen interpretation visible while keeping it distinct from the unresolved account of the graph’s earliest origin.

limitations.text: The earliest form of 包 remains unresolved. Shuowen’s pregnancy interpretation and the proposal that 包 developed from a graph depicting someone holding a child are competing accounts; this redraw does not establish an ancient form sequence.
The historical relationship between Shuowen’s pregnancy interpretation and the transmitted wrapping use has not been established.
